scope.description: Real 5-node in-memory cluster (A..E, ProtocolVersion 3, default timeouts scaled to 50ms) whose node A is restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs after a committed configuration change that is newer than A's last snapshot, then partitioned into {A,C} and {B,D,E}; every node of this deployment runs with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled so the commit index that the restart reads is the one the running protocol staged.
assumptions: Cluster state is produced through normal operations: BootstrapCluster({A,B,C}) from A, election, three committed applies, a user-triggered Snapshot on A, AddVoter(D) and AddVoter(E), and one further committed apply; no log entry, snapshot or index is written by the harness.

A is shut down (graceful Shutdown) rather than crashed, and its store objects (log store, stable store, snapshot store) are reused for the restart; the in-memory transports are reconnected so that the restarted A can reach only C.
The partition is expressed only by transport disconnection in both directions; the Raft fault model, RPC lifecycles and election timing are untouched.

All five nodes run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled from the start, which is the deployment mode whose restart behaviour is under test; the harness also records that disabling it during the first life leaves the stored commit index at 0.
The cluster is stopped at the end of the test; the observation window uses the nodes' own election timeouts plus a bounded wait for both partitions to elect.
excluded: No process crash or storage fault is injected: A is shut down gracefully and its stores are reused intact.
No on-disk log store is exercised; only the in-memory CommitTrackingLogStore.
The conflicting commits are observed at the two leaders; the loss of the minority entry after healing is not executed.

basis.prefix: The harness creates five InmemTransports with addresses A..E, a full mesh of connections, and per node an InmemStore (stable), InmemCommitTrackingStore (logs) and InmemSnapshotStore (snapshots). It calls BootstrapCluster(confA, logsA, stableA, snapsA, transA, {A,B,C}), then NewRaft for A, B and C with MockFSM and Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true; it waits for a leader, transfers leadership to A if another node won, applies three commands, waits on a Barrier and takes a user snapshot on A (snapshot index 6, configuration {A,B,C}). It then starts D and E with empty stores and calls AddVoter on the leader for each of them, followed by one more applied command so every follower stages a commit index at or above the new configuration entry (index 8). It emits a 'fixture' event with the snapshot index, the newest configuration entry index and membership, the stored commit index, the pre-restart configuration A reports and the derived operands commit_covers_config_entry and snapshot_before_config_entry. It shuts A down, cuts the transports so that {A,C} cannot reach {B,D,E}, creates a fresh transport for A connected only to C, and restarts A from its own stores with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true, emitting a 'restart' event with A's state, last applied index and reported configuration. It then waits for a leader in each partition and emits an 'outcome' event with the leaders and terms per partition, the leader count, whether each node in the minority partition is leader, the configurations reported by the restarted A, by C and by the majority leader, the result of an Apply submitted to each leader, the index and term each committed at, the two committed payloads and a derived conflicting_commits operand. Event order: fixture, restart, outcome.
basis.responsibility: hashicorp/raft NewRaft configuration scan combined with the RestoreCommittedLogs replay: the restarted node is responsible for deriving candidate admission and election quorum from the latest configuration entry in its own log, and voters are responsible for granting at most the votes their own view of the configuration requires.

comparisons.description: The restarted node's live configuration should be the membership of the committed configuration entry in its own log; this is the same predicate the earlier supplied-fixture experiment declared, here with stores produced by real operations.
A node whose effective configuration holds two of the five voters of the configuration recorded in its own committed log must not reach Leader while it can reach only one of those voters.
The cluster should have at most one leader; both partitions observed here are disjoint halves of one cluster.
Two leaders must not commit different entries at the same index and term.
A leader holding only a minority of the current voter set must not be able to commit an entry.
In-partition control: node C, whose configuration is the current one, must not become leader in the same two-voter partition.
The rest of the cluster still reports the current five-voter configuration, so the two sides disagree about membership while both lead.

knowledge.assertion: the persisted commit index exists only when the node ran with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled
